DIY-Thermocam 4.0 brings new firmware, Studio for your computer, and the V4 camera you can build from an assembled main board and off-the-shelf modules.

## Downloads

| | File |
| --- | --- |
| **Studio for macOS** (Apple silicon and Intel) | `DIY-Thermocam-Studio-macOS.dmg` |
| **Studio for Windows** 10 and 11 | `DIY-Thermocam-Studio-Windows.exe` |
| **Studio for Linux** (x86-64) | `DIY-Thermocam-Studio-Linux.AppImage` or `.deb` |
| **Firmware 4.0** for V3 and V4 cameras (Teensy 4.1) | `firmware.hex` |

Install the firmware from Studio: **Camera › Update firmware…**, then choose `firmware.hex`. V1 and V2 cameras stay on [firmware 2.5.0](https://github.com/maxritter/diy-thermocam/releases/tag/2.5.0). On Linux, [allow USB access](https://github.com/maxritter/diy-thermocam/blob/master/docs/manual.md#linux-usb-permissions) first.

## What's new

- **Studio** for macOS, Windows and Linux: measure boxes, spots and lines on the live image, record, export MP4, GIF and TIFF, and open the camera's microSD card.
- **Firmware 4.0** with a faster USB connection (8.77 frames per second over USB) and microSD reads at 9.2 MB/s.
- **V4 hardware**: an assembled main board, FLIR Lepton Breakout Board V2.0, a printed shell or a laser-cut acrylic case, and a [build guide](https://github.com/maxritter/diy-thermocam/blob/master/docs/building-instructions.md) with no soldering.

V4 is experimental: its boards and case haven't been tested on a real camera yet. A V3 runs firmware 4.0 and Studio today.

The full list is in the [changelog](https://github.com/maxritter/diy-thermocam/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md). `SHA256SUMS.txt` lists a checksum for every file.
